subject: Physics
source: IISER IAT 2018 question paper (English, scanned), iiseradmission.in
_transcription: Physics = pages p09-p11 (printed page numbers 11-13) under the 'Physics' heading: Q46-Q51 on p09, Q52-Q58 on p10, Q59-Q60 on p11 (rest of p11 blank). The paper numbers its 60 questions straight through, so Physics' printed numbers 46-60 are restarted as ref/questionNumber 1-15 (printed 46 = ref 1 ... printed 60 = ref 15). Numbers checked unbroken 46..60 against the printed 'N.' labels; no question runs over a page. Scan with no text layer, transcribed from the 150 dpi render with 4x zooms of every figure and of Q59's options; the faint mirror-image show-through from the back of each sheet was ignored. Two-column option blocks (Q46, Q47, Q51, Q55, Q59) put A and B in the left column and C and D in the right, confirmed by the printed letters; options are listed A-D. Q55's option B wraps its last syllable ('tion.') to the top of the right column. No answer key. Stem figures: Q49, Q50, Q53, Q58, Q60; Q56's options are graphs.

rows.text: A cylindrical vessel of radius 5 cm is filled with water up to a height of 20 cm. The cylinder is open to atmosphere at the top. A small aperture of radius 2 mm is made on the side of the cylinder at a height of 5 cm from the bottom of the vessel. For approximately how long will water leak out of the aperture?

Two simple pendulums of length 1 m each, with bobs having masses 1 kg and 2 kg, are hanging from the ceiling of an elevator. The elevator starts moving vertically downwards with acceleration \(g/10\). Assuming \(g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}\), approximately what are the time periods of the two pendulums?
What is the probability that a radioactive nucleus will not have decayed after a time equal to twice its half-life?

rows.subtopic: Electric Dipole and Dipole in a Uniform Field
rows.text: An electric dipole having point charges \(+q\) and \(-q\), separated by a fixed distance \(d\) is kept under the influence of a uniform electric field \(\mathbf{E}\), such that the axis of the dipole is making an angle \(\theta = 45^\circ\) with the direction of \(\mathbf{E}\), as shown in the figure. If the electric dipole is allowed to rotate in the \(xy\)-plane with its center being stationary, what is the magnitude of the net torque acting on the electric dipole?

figure.note: Axes: vertical y-axis with an arrow labelled E (field along +y), horizontal dashed x-axis. A dipole passes through the origin at an angle: charge +q upper right, charge -q lower left. The angle theta is marked between the y-axis (E) and the dipole axis; a dashed bracket alongside the dipole is labelled d.

rows.text: In the circuit shown, what is the approximate current passing through the resistor \(R_3\)?

figure.note: Upper loop: a 6 V cell in the top wire and resistor R1 = 8 ohm on the right side with current I1 marked downward. Below a common horizontal wire, three parallel branches run down to a common bottom wire: left branch R2 = 10 ohm with a 10 V cell, current I2 marked upward; middle branch R3 = 5 ohm with a 3 V cell, current I3 marked downward; right branch R4 = 6 ohm with a 6 V cell, current I4 marked upward.

rows.text: An electromagnetic wave propagates along \(z\)-direction. The corresponding electric field is along \(x\)-direction. Which of the following is an acceptable direction for the magnetic field, considering \(\hat{x}\), \(\hat{y}\), and \(\hat{z}\) to be the unit vectors in a Cartesian co-ordinate system?

An iron ring of radius 2.1 m is to be fitted on top of the rim of a wheel of radius 2.121 m. The coefficient of volume expansion for iron is \(3.6 \times 10^{-5}\ \mathrm{K^{-1}}\). By approximately how much should the temperature of the iron ring be increased so that it fits the rim of the wheel?

An object of mass 100 g is sliding under gravity from point A to point B on a frictionless slide from a height of 5 m, as shown in the figure. After what distance will the object stop on the following flat track beyond point B if the coefficient of kinetic friction between the flat track and the object is 0.5?

figure.note: A block at point A at the top of a curved slide; a dotted vertical arrow beside it labelled 5 m down to the ground. The slide curves down (arrows along it) to point B on the flat ground, then the flat track continues to the right with arrows showing the motion.

rows.subtopic: Ampere's Circuital Law and the Solenoid
rows.text: A current of 45 A is passing through an infinitely long wire which lies along the axis of an infinitely long solenoid of radius 1 cm. The magnetic field produced by the solenoid in the direction of the current in the wire is 4 mT. What is the approximate magnitude of the resultant magnetic field at a point 3 mm radially away from the solenoid axis? (Use \(\mu_o = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\) T m/A.)

rows.chapter: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
rows.text: For a \(p\)-\(n\) junction normal diode and a Zener diode, which of the following statements is true?
options: The Zener diode has thicker depletion region and normal diode has higher electric field across the junction.
The normal diode has thicker depletion region and Zener diode has higher electric field across the junction.
The Zener diode has thicker depletion region and higher electric field across the junction.
The normal diode has thicker depletion region and higher electric field across the junction.

rows.text: Starting from rest, a car moves with a constant acceleration, and comes to a momentary stop with the same constant deceleration. Subsequently, it reverses its motion and returns to its original position in a similar manner. Which one of the following graphs of momentum (\(p\)) versus time (\(t\)) best describes the motion of the car?
options: p rises linearly from zero to a single peak, then falls linearly back to zero (one triangle above the t-axis)
p rises linearly from zero to a maximum, drops vertically to a negative minimum, then rises linearly back to zero
p rises linearly from zero to a maximum, falls linearly through zero to a negative minimum, then rises linearly back to zero
p rises linearly to a peak, falls to zero, then rises to a second equal peak and falls to zero again (two triangles above the t-axis)

rows.subtopic: Line Spectra of the Hydrogen Atom
rows.text: \(\lambda_2\) and \(\lambda_4\) are the wavelengths of photons required to excite the Hydrogen atom from its ground state to its second and fourth excited states, respectively. What is the correct ratio \(\lambda_2/\lambda_4\)?

A jeweler is holding a gold chain of uniform mass per unit length hanging vertically just above a weighing scale as shown in the figure. He offers to charge the customer for half of the maximum reading of the scale, after he releases the chain. What percentage more than the actual price does the customer pay if he agrees to the offer?

figure.note: A hand holds a chain hanging vertically, its lower end just above a digital weighing scale; the scale's display reads 00:00 gm beside a power symbol.

rows.text: A planet of mass \(m\) moves in an elliptical path around the Sun (which is at one of the foci of the ellipse), so that its maximum and minimum distances from the Sun are \(r_{\text{max}}\) and \(r_{\text{min}}\), respectively. Taking the gravitational constant to be \(G\) and the mass of the Sun to be \(M_s\), what is the angular momentum of the planet relative to the center of the Sun?

rows.subtopic: Addition, Subtraction and Resolution of Vectors
rows.text: Two posts of heights 20 m and 10 m are 60 m apart, as shown in the figure. Food grains are continuously distributed between the two posts. A crow sitting on top of the taller post wants to pick up a grain and sit on the other post. What should be the distance of the grain it picks from the bottom of the taller post to minimize the total flight length?

figure.note: A crow sits on top of a taller post on the left marked 20 m; a shorter post on the right marked 10 m; grains lie in a row along the ground between the posts; a double arrow along the ground between the posts is labelled 60 m.
